instruction: Open 'character.png' in GIMP and convert the image to grayscale mode, then save it as 'character_gray.png'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening character.png in GIMP, converting to grayscale (Image > Mode > Grayscale), and saving as character_gray.png. Evaluator checks that the output image is in grayscale mode (PIL mode 'L').

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts image mode using PIL Image.open() and returns img.mode
Metric correctly compares result mode with expected mode 'L' using exact string matching
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies both grayscale conversion (mode='L') and file save (path check)
Expected value 'L' is semantically correct - PIL mode 'L' represents grayscale (8-bit pixels, black and white)
Data flow is correct: getter extracts mode string -> metric compares with expected 'L' -> returns 1.0/0.0
No UI state dependencies - verification only requires file system access to saved image
Correct parameter handling: expected.get('mode') directly accesses the rules dict (framework calls get_rule which returns config['rules'])
Will work correctly at runtime - PIL can reliably read image mode from saved PNG files
